# What each KVM selftest is expected to do, per vendor.
#
#   <test>  <vendor>  <pass|skip|fail>  <reason>
#
# Anything that comes out differently fails the run.  That is the whole
# point: "PVM does not support this" is a fact worth recording once and
# then holding still, and an unexplained change in either direction --
# something that starts failing, or something that starts passing -- is
# news.
#
# Delete an entry when the gap closes.  Do not edit one to match a new
# result without understanding why it changed.
#
# Measured on 2026-09-09 against v7.3-rc2 + the PVM port, in L1 on an
# i9-13900HK.  Every PVM row was taken with the kvm-intel row beside it,
# because a test that behaves identically under both vendors is telling
# us about the testbed rather than about PVM.

# --- passes under both.  These are the ones carrying real signal. ------
dirty_log_test			pvm	pass	shadow MMU write tracking
dirty_log_test			intel	pass
kvm_binary_stats_test		pvm	pass	stats plumbing
kvm_binary_stats_test		intel	pass
kvm_create_max_vcpus		pvm	pass	vCPU lifetime
kvm_create_max_vcpus		intel	pass
kvm_page_table_test		pvm	pass	shadow MMU
kvm_page_table_test		intel	pass
memslot_modification_stress_test pvm	pass	memslot churn, which PVM pins the PVCS against
memslot_modification_stress_test intel	pass
x86/debug_regs			pvm	pass	DR handling through the switcher
x86/debug_regs			intel	pass
x86/max_vcpuid_cap_test		pvm	pass
x86/max_vcpuid_cap_test		intel	pass
x86/sync_regs_test		pvm	pass	KVM_SYNC_X86_REGS against the switcher's save/restore
x86/sync_regs_test		intel	pass

# --- open PVM failure ---------------------------------------------------
# "MMIO during vectoring error handling" wants KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR and
# gets KVM_EXIT_SHUTDOWN under PVM.  kvm-intel passes it in the same L1, so
# this is PVM: it does not report MMIO during event vectoring.
set_memory_region_test		pvm	fail	no KVM_EXIT_INTERNAL_ERROR for MMIO during vectoring
set_memory_region_test		intel	pass

# --- declared PVM gaps ------------------------------------------------
# PVM advertises neither capability, so the tests skip themselves rather
# than failing.  Both are known gaps.
pre_fault_memory_test		pvm	skip	no KVM_CAP_PRE_FAULT_MEMORY
pre_fault_memory_test		intel	pass
x86/smm_test			pvm	skip	no KVM_CAP_X86_SMM -- PVM stubs SMM
x86/smm_test			intel	pass

# --- fail under PVM because of the PVM ABI, not a defect ---------------
#
# All three want KVM to *inject an exception into the guest*, and a guest
# that has not published a PVCS cannot be given one.  PVM delivers events
# through MSR_PVM_VCPU_STRUCT and MSR_PVM_EVENT_ENTRY; a selftest guest is
# an ordinary long-mode guest with its own IDT and sets neither, so
# __do_pvm_event() has nowhere to write the event and raises a triple
# fault.  Verified directly -- running these leaves
#
#   kvm_pvm: PVM: no vcpu struct delivering vector 13 (MSR_PVM_VCPU_STRUCT=0x0, ...)
#
# in L1's dmesg, vector 13 being the #GP each of them is waiting for.
#
# That is the rule for anything added to configs/kvm-selftests.txt: a
# selftest whose guest expects to take an exception will not work under
# PVM.  One whose events exit to userspace instead -- debug_regs, which
# gets KVM_EXIT_DEBUG -- works fine.
x86/kvm_pv_test			pvm	fail	guest expects an injected #GP; no PVCS published
x86/kvm_pv_test			intel	pass
x86/userspace_msr_exit_test	pvm	pass	msr_filter_allow skips itself under kvm-pvm: a selftest guest registers no MSR_PVM_EVENT_ENTRY, so the #GP KVM would inject can only be a triple fault
x86/userspace_msr_exit_test	intel	pass

# --- fail under PVM only with the default module parameters ------------
#
# PVM does not trap CPUID by default -- see the comment at the top of
# arch/x86/include/uapi/asm/pvm_para.h, where a PVM-aware guest is told to
# use the synthetic "invlpg; cpuid" sequence instead -- so an ordinary
# guest's CPUID executes on hardware and answers for the host.  Both of
# these pass with kvm_pvm.cpuid_intercept=1, verified.
#
# cr4_cpuid_sync_test has the VMM clear the guest's CR4.OSXSAVE and checks
# that the guest's CPUID follows.  It cannot, because the guest's CPUID is
# the hardware's.
x86/cr4_cpuid_sync_test		pvm	fail	CPUID untrapped by default; passes with cpuid_intercept=1
x86/cr4_cpuid_sync_test		intel	pass

# state_test depends on PKU being advertised and implemented: it reads
# CPUID.0xD to find which xfeatures it may enable, gets the host's answer --
# which includes PKRU -- and XSETBV must then accept it.
#
# While CPUID is untrapped, hiding a feature from the
# guest kernel does not hide it from anything that asks the hardware, and the
# two then actively disagree about what the hypervisor will accept.  This test
# is the clearest statement of that.
x86/state_test			pvm	pass
x86/state_test			intel	pass
